Bismarck engaging Hood, Battle of the Denmark Strait. Seen from Prinz Eugen. [GYFY][1280x720]

Here is a link to a detailed account of the battle. Ignoring the fact that Hood never should have been sent to engage a battleship, the British had two other factors that may have made a big difference: their approach and their rangefinders.

The British did not put as much stock in centralized fire-control as other nations, so their primary rangefinders were relatively small, therefore relatively inaccurate. Instead, they preferred to have each turret be controlled locally. In this case, the British ships kept Bismarck nearly on the bow - so the forward turrets' rangefinders were obscured by spray.
Bismarck engaging Hood, Battle of the Denmark Strait. Seen from Prinz Eugen. [cross-post /v/warshippix]

For those interested, here is a very detailed account of the battle. (Archive, the live site has less info.) The short version: the Brits engaged from an inferior position, with inferior equipment, with one ship that really shouldn't have been there.
